about: Hand-checked notes: what newer or more direct primary sources say about a UN figure on the site. Each note names its sources, quotes the numbers it uses, and has the date it was checked. Process and rules: docs/CROSS-CHECK-PROCESS.md. Evidence for these entries: docs/DATA-CROSS-CHECK.md.

AFG.text: Afghanistan's statistics office (NSIA) estimates 36.4 million people for the year 2025-26. The UN's figure for mid-2025 is 43.8 million, 20% higher. Neither is a count: the last census was in 1979, and NSIA's figure is a projection forward from a 2003-05 household listing.

figure.what: NSIA estimate of the population living in Afghanistan, solar year 1404 (2025-26)

unFigure.what: UN population on 1 July 2025 (forecast)

links.label: National Statistics and Information Authority (NSIA), Estimated Population of Afghanistan 2025-26, September 2025

quotes.text: The total population of the country in 1404 (2025-26) is estimated to be about 36.4 million persons, of which around 18.6 million persons (51.0%) are males and 17.8 million persons (49.0%) are females
The Population Estimates publication of 1404 (2025-26) has been prepared based on the data obtained from household listing of 1381-1384 (2003-05), using the (Pt = P0 ert) formula.
Due to the existence of security and economic problems, the second complete population census of the country after the population census of 1358 has not yet been conducted

AFG.text: UNHCR counted 2.9 million Afghans returning from Iran and Pakistan in 2025, and 1.37 million more in 2026 up to 24 October. The UN forecast that about 74,000 more people would leave than arrive in 2025. These returns, many of them deportations, add people the forecast does not include.

figure.what: Afghans who returned to Afghanistan from Iran and Pakistan in 2025 (UNHCR); 1,366,140 more returned in 2026 up to 24 October

unFigure.what: UN net migration in 2025 (forecast)

quotes.text: So far this year, nearly 150,000 Afghans have returned from Iran and Pakistan. These arrivals come on top of already unprecedented returns – 2.9 million people in 2025, bringing the total to some 5.4 million since October 2023.

AGO.text: Angola's 2024 census, published by its statistics office (INE) in November 2025, found 36.6 million people on 19 September 2024. That total already adds back people a follow-up survey showed the census had missed. The UN's figure for mid-2024 is 37.9 million, about 3.5% higher, and higher still by the census date.

figure.what: People living in Angola, 2024 census final result (adjusted for missed people)

unFigure.what: UN forecast of Angola's population on 1 July 2024 (about 38.1 million by 19 September 2024)

quotes.text: Os resultados definitivos do Censo 2024 mostram que , em 19 de Setembro de 2024 (momento censitário), a população residente em Angola era de 36 604 681 habitantes, sendo 17 931 985 homens, representando 49% da população total , e 18 672 69 6 mulheres, representando 51%.

O erro líquido de subcobertura do Censo para a população apresentou uma taxa de 28,3% a nível nacional. Isto significa que, sem o ajuste do IC, o Censo teria subestimado a população em quase um terço.

A avaliação da qualidade do Censo de 2024, através do Inquérito de Cobertura (IC) de 2025, foi essencial para corrigir os erros de subcobertura e obter uma contagem populacional fidedigna, utilizando o Método de Estimação por Sistema Dual.

BGD.text: The Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics estimates 174.81 million people on 31 December 2025, building on its 2022 census (169.83 million after correcting for people missed). The UN's figure for the same moment is about 176.75 million, 1.1% higher, so the two match.

It is noted from the data that in 2022 census, the total enumerated population is recorded as 16,51,58,616 and the adjusted population, 16,98,28,911.

BGD.text: UNHCR counted 1,206,500 refugees and asylum-seekers from Myanmar, mostly Rohingya, in Bangladesh on 30 September 2026, close to the UN's 1.25 million people born in Myanmar. CHN.text: China's statistics office counted 1,404.89 million people at the end of 2025, 3.39 million fewer than a year before. The UN's figure for the same moment is about 1,414.5 million, 0.7% higher, so the two match.

figure.what: national population of mainland China at year-end (excludes Hong Kong, Macao, Taiwan and foreigners)

unFigure.what: average of the UN's 1 July 2025 and 1 July 2026 forecasts (1,416,096,094 and 1,412,914,089), standing in for 1 January 2026

quotes.text: By the end of 2025, the total number of national population [5] reached 1,404.89 million, a decrease of 3.39 million over that at the end of 2024.

[5] The national population refers to the population of the 31 provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the central government and servicemen of the Chinese mainland, excluding residents of Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan and foreigners

CHN.text: China counted 7.92 million births in 2025. The UN forecast 8.71 million, about 10% more. A year earlier it went the other way: China counted 9.54 million births in 2024 against the UN's 8.82 million, so the UN's birth figures for these years are less certain than its population total.

figure.what: births registered in 2025

unFigure.what: UN forecast of births in 2025

quotes.text: There were 7.92 million births in 2025 with a crude birth rate of 5.63 per thousand; and there were 11.31 million deaths with a crude death rate of 8.04 per thousand.
There were 9.54 million births in 2024 with a crude birth rate of 6.77 per thousand; and there were 10.93 million deaths with a crude death rate of 7.76 per thousand.

CHN.text: China's 2020 census registered 1,430,695 people from abroad living on the mainland: 845,697 foreigners plus residents from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan. That counts nationality, not country of birth. The UN puts people born abroad at 1.64 million in mid-2024, a similar size.

CMR.text: Cameroon's census office (BUCREP) estimated 28.9 million people in 2023; the UN's mid-2023 figure, 28.4 million, is 1.7% lower. A new census finished counting on 15 September 2026 with 22.8 million people registered, about 80% of the 30.1 million expected; final results will follow a check survey.

EGY.text: Egypt's statistics agency CAPMAS says the population inside the country reached 109 million on 9 May 2026. Its clock adds births and subtracts deaths from health-ministry records. The UN's figure for that date is about 119.8 million, about 10% higher.

وكان عدد السكان قد بلغ (108 مليون نسمة) يــوم السبت الموافق 16/8/2025 وفقاً لما أعلنته الساعة السكانية بالجهاز المركزي للتعبئة العامة والإحصاء المرتبطة بقاعدة بيانات تسجيل المواليد والوفيات بوزارة الصحة والسكان.

EGY.text: UNHCR had 1,098,708 refugees and asylum-seekers registered in Egypt on 30 June 2026, 851,947 of them from Sudan. That is already 96% of the UN's figure of 1.14 million people born abroad in mid-2024, which also has to cover migrant workers and other foreigners.

quotes.text: As of 30 June, the registered refugees and asylum-seekers population in Egypt stood at 1,098,708 individuals, including those who arrived in Egypt before the conflict. Sudanese nationals constitute the largest group at 851,947 individuals (78 per cent), followed by other nationalities at 152,882 (14 per cent).
Returns to Sudan from neighbouring countries since 2024 reached 1.12 million, with 61,055 people recorded entering Sudan from Egypt in June alone.

IDN.text: Indonesia's statistics office (BPS) found 284.67 million people in its 2025 intercensal population survey, SUPAS 2025, released in May 2026, after the UN's 2024 figures were made. The UN's mid-2025 figure is 285.72 million, 0.4% higher: the two match.

figure.what: population of Indonesia from the SUPAS 2025 survey, mid-2025

unFigure.what: UN forecast for 1 July 2025

links.label: BPS-Statistics Indonesia, Berita Resmi Statistik No. 51/05/Th. XXIX: Hasil Survei Penduduk Antar Sensus (SUPAS 2025), 5 May 2026

quotes.text: Jumlah penduduk Indonesia hasil SUPAS 2025 mencapai 284,67 juta jiwa. Selama periode 2010–2025, jumlah penduduk mengalami peningkatan dari 237,64 juta jiwa hasil SP2010 menjadi 284,67 juta jiwa hasil SUPAS 2025.

IDN.text: The SUPAS 2025 survey found about 537,000 people moved to Indonesia and about one million left over 2022–2025, a net loss of 53 people per 100,000 each year, roughly 150,000 a year. The UN shows a net loss of only about 38,000 a year, so the survey points to more people leaving.

figure.what: net international migration per year, 2022–2025: survey rate of −53 per 100,000 people a year applied to 284.67 million (our arithmetic)

unFigure.what: UN net migration forecast for 2024 (2022 and 2023 estimates: −37,501 each)

links.label: BPS-Statistics Indonesia, Berita Resmi Statistik No. 51/05/Th. XXIX: Hasil Survei Penduduk Antar Sensus (SUPAS 2025), 5 May 2026

quotes.text: Hasil SUPAS 2025 menunjukkan bahwa angka migrasi masuk internasional tercatat sebesar 0,61 (rata-rata 61 orang masuk ke Indonesia per 100.000 penduduk tiap tahun) atau mencapai 537 ribu migran internasional yang masuk ke Indonesia pada periode 2022–2025. Pada periode yang sama, angka migrasi keluar internasional adalah sebesar 1,14 (rata-rata 114 orang keluar dari Indonesia per 100.000 penduduk tiap tahun) atau sebanyak satu juta orang migran keluar dari Indonesia.
Angka migrasi neto internasional tercatat sebesar –0,53. Hal tersebut berarti ada pengurangan rata-rata 53 orang setiap 100.000 penduduk Indonesia setiap tahunnya karena migrasi internasional.

IRN.text: UNHCR counted more than 1.9 million Afghans who returned or were deported from Iran to Afghanistan in 2025, and 581,600 more in 2026 up to 3 October. The UN's forecast shows Iran gaining about 117,000 people from migration in 2025, so it misses this large outflow.

quotes.text: In 2025, more than 1.9 million Afghans returned or were deported from Iran – many not by choice. In 2026, a further 581,600 Afghans have returned.
Over 5 million Afghans returned from neighbouring countries over the past two years – almost 1.9 million from Iran in 2025 alone.

IRN.text: UNHCR counts 1.65 million refugees and others in need of protection in Iran in 2026. That is a narrower group than the UN's 3.84 million people born abroad in mid-2024. Almost 1.9 million Afghans also returned or were deported from Iran in 2025.

LBN.text: UNHCR estimates 630,697 Syrians returned to Syria from Lebanon between 8 December 2024 and 30 April 2026. The UN's forecast shows Lebanon losing about 17,000 people to migration in 2024 and 10,000 in 2025, and counts 785,000 Syria-born residents in mid-2024, before these returns. LBN.text: Lebanon's statistics office surveyed 39,000 households and estimated 4.842 million residents in mid-2018, not counting refugee camps, army barracks or informal settlements; 20% were not Lebanese citizens. The UN's 2018 figure is 5.98 million. The two are not directly comparable.

Eighty per cent of residents are Lebanese and 20 per cent are citizens of other countries.

MMR.text: Myanmar's 2024 census (provisional results) puts the population at 51.3 million on 30 September 2024. The UN's figure for that date is about 54.6 million, 6% higher. The census counted only 32.2 million people in person; the other 19.1 million is an estimate, made with remote-sensing technology, for areas where counting was not possible.

quotes.text: Total population (2026) 35.3M People in need
An estimated 18.3 million people19 (52 per cent of the population) face acute food insecurity.

YEM.text: UNHCR counts 65,308 refugees and asylum-seekers in Yemen (August 2026), mostly from Somalia and Ethiopia. An IOM report cites about 132,300 stranded migrants, a figure from the January 2025 humanitarian plan. The UN counts 393,000 people born abroad (mid-2024), 285,000 of them born in Somalia. These count different groups.

While the number of stranded migrants in Yemen is difficult to estimate, the January 2025 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan indicates approximately 132,300 stranded migrants in the country.

YEM.text: IOM tracked 107,900 migrant arrivals in Yemen from the Horn of Africa in 2025, up from 60,900 in 2024, even though data collection was suspended from May to July 2025. These are arrivals only, not net migration. The UN puts net migration at about 16,000 more people leaving than arriving in 2025.
